strings: The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh.

Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur.

Beyond its fearsome inhabitants, the twisting tunnels of the Grizzled Den draw opportunists searching for natural wealth. Prospectors frequently venture past the outer entrance to hammer at copper veins jutting from the frozen stone walls, while adventurous scouts often scour the darker corners for discarded footlockers. However, delve too far into the inner reaches, and you are bound to face the dens' largest and most vicious predators lurking in the shadows.

With direct zeppelin towers linking to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, it stands as an armed staging ground against local jungle troll tribes and hostile Alliance forces.

Grommash Hold is the fortified seat of Warchief Thrall, nestled high in the red cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Grommash Hellscream's sacrifice, the fortress serves as the command center and political heart of the new Horde.

Growless Cave is a frigid cavern carved into the crags of the Alterac Mountains, overrun by ferocious mountain yetis. It is best known as the resting place of the Flame of Uzel, an unholy ceremonial pyre tied to the dark necromancy of Helcular.

Beyond the primal danger of the beasts, the cave harbors a sinister past: inside lies the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left behind by the ambitious human mage Helcular. Gurubashi Arena is an ancient stone colosseum standing in southern Stranglethorn Vale, originally built by the mighty Gurubashi Empire. In the present day, it serves as a chaotic free-for-all proving ground where pirates and wandering brawlers shed blood over locked chests of treasure.

Long before human or orc set foot in Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi Arena—known also as the Great Arena—was built as a monument to martial strength by the sprawling Gurubashi troll empire. In ancient days, champions fought to the death upon its sands until the earth was slick with troll blood. Once every generation, tradition dictates that the greatest troll warriors across Azeroth gather within these towering stone walls to duel for the honor of their loa, presided over by King Rastakhan of the Zandalari. To win this rite is among the highest honors a troll warrior can attain.

Though the empire has long since fractured into warring tribes, the arena's floor never stays clean for long. Today, lawless buccaneers and ruffians oversee a different sort of bloody spectacle. A pirate named Short John Mithril oversees the grounds, where every few hours a chest of plundered booty is hauled into the center of the ring. Anyone who steps onto the floor is fair game—faction allegiances vanish, and combatants must butcher their way to the prize against all comers.
